title: Personal Credit Cards: points needed to bring an overdrawn autopay source back to zero
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: points needed to restore an overdrawn autopay source

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line. When rewards points on a card are used to bring the card's overdrawn autopay source checking account back to zero, it converts the overdrawn amount of that checking account into the number of points needed.

## Rule

1. The points needed are the overdrawn amount divided by the card tier's cash value per point.
2. The quotient is rounded up to the next whole point. A quotient that is already a whole number stays as it is.
3. The value per point used is the card tier's cash value per point, the value that applies when points are redeemed as a deposit.

## Calculation steps

1. Take the overdrawn amount of the autopay source checking account.
2. Divide it by the card tier's cash value per point.
3. If the quotient has any fraction of a point, raise it to the next whole point.

## Worked examples (hypothetical value per point of 0.03 USD, not a tier value)

| Overdrawn amount | Quotient | Points needed |
|---|---|---|
| 43.27 USD | 1442.33 | 1443 |
| 43.20 USD | 1440 exactly | 1440 |
| 0.01 USD | 0.33 | 1 |

## Wrong reading and correct basis

- **Wrong:** round the quotient to the nearest point, giving 1442 for 43.27 USD. **Correct:** round up, giving 1443, so the deposit is not short of the overdrawn amount.
- **Wrong:** drop the fraction, giving 1442. **Correct:** round up to 1443.
- **Wrong:** add one point even when the quotient is whole. **Correct:** a whole quotient, such as 1440, stays as it is.
